# AIVA Module

The unified macOS bridge binary, exposed as the `macos` command. Single signed gateway to all macOS system services.

## Why this exists

Every macOS module used to shell out to its own CLIs (`security`, `osascript`, `afplay`, `pgrep`, `launchctl`, `mdfind`, `say`...). That meant TCC permission prompts scattered across many binaries, keychain ACL prompts re-triggered by every binary rebuild, and every module re-implementing the same boilerplate. Now there is one signed binary, everything routes through it.

## Rule for module authors

If you need to read or change anything on macOS, call the `macos` binary. Do not shell out to:

| Don't use | Use instead |
|---|---|
| `security find/add/delete-generic-password`, `security unlock-keychain` | `macos keychain get/set/delete/list/unlock` |
| `osascript -e 'tell Messages...'` | `macos messages send` |
| `osascript -e 'set volume...'` | `macos system volume` |
| `say "text"` | `macos say "text"` |
| `afplay file.aiff` | `macos audio play file.aiff` |
| `pgrep -x Finder` | `macos system running Finder` |
| `pgrep -f pattern` | `macos system running pattern --pattern` |
| `launchctl list/bootstrap/bootout/kickstart` | `macos system launchctl-list/load/unload/kickstart` |
| `mdfind`, `tag` | `macos spotlight search/find-by-tag/list-tags/tags/set-tags` |
| EventKit / Contacts / Notes via AppleScript or direct sqlite | `macos calendar/reminders/contacts/notes` |
| Maps URL building | `macos maps search/geocode/directions` |

If a CLI you need is missing, add a subcommand to the binary instead of shelling out from your module.

## Commands

```
macos messages    search | read | unanswered | thread | send | tapback
macos calendar    list-calendars | list | search | show | create | update | delete
macos reminders   lists | list | show | search | create | complete | uncomplete | edit | delete | create-list | delete-list
macos contacts    search | show | list | add-email | add-phone | add-url | delete-url | add-social | delete-social | add-im | delete-im | set-company | set-note | backup
macos notes       list | show | search | folders | create | update | delete
macos maps        search | geocode | reverse-geocode | directions
macos say         <text> [--voice V] [--rate R] [--output PATH] [--list-voices]
macos keychain    get | set | delete | list | unlock
macos spotlight   search | metadata | tags | set-tags | add-tags | remove-tags | find-by-tag | list-tags
macos system      ps | running | open | launchctl-list | launchctl-load | launchctl-unload | launchctl-kickstart | volume | volume-get | display
macos audio       play | devices
```

All commands return JSON on stdout. Errors return JSON `{"error": "..."}` with non-zero exit.

## Layout

- Source: `src/` (Swift, organized by domain)
- Binary: `bin/AIVA-MacOS.app/Contents/MacOS/aiva` (the actual signed binary)
- Public command: `macos` (symlink at `~/.aiva/state/bin/macos`)
- Build script: `./build.sh`

## Signing

The binary is signed with `Developer ID Application: Michael Shaffer (6D4T7VB2AF)`. Team ID `6D4T7VB2AF` is stable across rebuilds, so keychain ACL partition list entries keep working.

When you add a new keychain item that the bridge will read, set its partition list once:

```
security set-generic-password-partition-list \
  -S "apple-tool:,apple:,teamid:6D4T7VB2AF" \
  -k '<login_password>' \
  -s SERVICE_NAME -a aiva \
  ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db
```

Or simpler: create the item using `macos keychain set`, the bridge ends up on the ACL from the start.

## Build

```
cd ~/.aiva/modules/aiva
./build.sh
```

`build.sh` runs `swift build -c release`, copies into the app bundle, and signs with the Developer ID cert. Always use the script, do not run `codesign --sign -` directly. Ad-hoc signing produces a new CDHash every build, which invalidates keychain ACL entries.

# Call History

Module-owned privileged reader for macOS CallHistoryDB.

## What It Owns

1. `privileged/callhistory.swift`, the Swift plugin code loaded by the AIVA bridge.
2. Read-only call history stats and listing operations exposed through the plugin namespace.
3. `bin/handler`, the public CLI layer for `aiva callhistory ...`.
4. A narrow refresh operation that posts Apple's CallHistory sync notifications, then polls the local database before returning.
5. The `cap:full-disk-access` requirement needed to read `~/Library/Application Support/CallHistoryDB/CallHistory.storedata`.

## Runtime

1. Machine: laptop.
2. Source database: `~/Library/Application Support/CallHistoryDB/CallHistory.storedata`.
3. Access mode: read-only SQLite through the bridge plugin.
4. Refresh mode: public handler posts `com.apple.callhistorysync.idslaunchnotification` and `com.apple.CallHistoryPluginHelper.launchnotification`, then re-reads the database.

## Verification

Use a read-only stats check:

```bash
aiva callhistory stats
```

The command should return total call counts and oldest or newest call timestamps.

For live questions where the iPhone may not have synced into the Mac database yet, refresh first:

```bash
aiva callhistory list --refresh --limit 10
```

The command should include a `refresh` object and current call rows.

When a row includes `location`, the handler also adds
`location_kind: "number_origin"` and `location_note`. This location is carrier
or phone-number origin metadata, not the person's current physical location.

If Apple has live call activity that has not landed in `CallHistoryDB`, the
`refresh.freshness` object reports `newer_callservice_activity: true` and
includes a warning. The callservicesd log redacts phone numbers, so this is a
freshness guard, not a second source for call details.

# Communications Pipeline Module

Date: 2026-04-23

## Purpose

End-to-end pipeline for processing Mike's incoming communications (email, iMessage, voicemails, Maricar's Google Chat) and producing reviewed drafts or auto-sent responses.

## What It Does

1. Scans Gmail work, Gmail personal, iMessages, Google Chat with Maricar, and voicemail-derived Gmail items deterministically
2. Filters spam (cold outreach, recruiters, vendor pitches)
3. Routes legitimate items to Mike or Maricar based on routing rules
4. Dispatches one-shot LLM drafters only after a deterministic action queue exists
5. Classifies each draft by tier (1=auto-send, 2=send+notify, 3=review)
6. Auto-sends Tier 1 items (signed "- AIVA" for Maricar messages)
7. Notifies Mike of pending drafts at 9:30 AM
8. Tracks every outcome for learning over time

## Architecture

```
                    +----------+
                    |  Inbox   |
                    +-----+----+
                          |
              +-----------+-----------+
              |   action-scan script  |  (module-owned Python, deterministic)
              |   - Scans live CLIs   |
              |   - Filters/routes    |
              |   - Dedupes state     |
              |   - Max 5 items       |
              +-----------+-----------+
                          |
                          v
              +------------------------+
              |  .action-queue.json    |
              +-----------+------------+
                          |
              +-----------+------------+
              |    Dispatcher          |  (bash, no AI)
              |    - Max 5 drafters    |
              |    - One per item      |
              |    - Records ledger    |
              +-----------+------------+
                          |
              +-----------+------------+
              |    Drafters (1-5)      |  (one-shot cron, glm-5.1)
              |    - Read DRAFTING.md  |
              |    - Verify channels   |
              |    - Cross-check       |
              |    - Classify tier     |
              +-----------+------------+
                          |
                          v
              +------------------------+
              |  .pending-drafts/      |
              +-----------+------------+
                          |
              +-----------+------------+
              |  Auto-Sender (9:30AM)  |  (bash, no AI)
              |  Sends Tier 1          |
              |  Forwards emails       |
              +-----------+------------+
                          |
                          v
              +------------------------+
              |  Draft Review Notify   |  (cron, 9:30 AM)
              |  Reports to Google     |
              |  Chat with summary     |
              +------------------------+
                          |
                          v
              Mike reviews in Google Chat
              "send 1, change 2, skip 3"
                          |
                          v
              +------------------------+
              |  Draft Tracker         |
              |  Archives outcomes     |
              |  Builds approval rates |
              +------------------------+
```

## Channel Types Supported

The dispatcher creates drafts for three response channels:

1. **email** — Reply to incoming email (`google gmail reply MSG_ID`)
2. **imessage** — Reply to iMessage (`ssh laptop "imessage send 'PHONE'"`)
3. **outbound_email** — Fresh email Mike needs to send (`google gmail send`)
4. **route_to_maricar** — Google Chat ping to Maricar + email forward (`google chat send` + `google gmail forward`)
5. **google_chat** — Drafted Google Chat reply from Mike to Maricar (`google chat send --stdin`)

## Tier Classification

Every draft gets a tier from the drafter (GLM-5.1 via OpenClaw cron with full context):

- **Tier 1 (AUTO-SEND)**: Acknowledgments, Maricar delegations, sub nudges. Zero risk of harm if sent. Auto-sent at 9:30 AM by auto-sender script.
- **Tier 2 (SEND WITH NOTIFICATION)**: Simple confirmations, scheduling when calendar is clear. Currently routed to review until track record builds, may auto-send later.
- **Tier 3 (DRAFT AND WAIT)**: Money, pricing, scope, contracts, new clients, judgment calls. Always requires Mike's approval.

## File Locations

### Scripts
- `~/.aiva/modules/comms-pipeline/bin/action-scan` — Deterministic scanner; writes the canonical queue
- `~/mikeshaffer/scripts/dispatch-drafters.sh` — Dispatcher (no AI, plumbing)
- `~/mikeshaffer/scripts/auto-sender.sh` — Auto-sender for Tier 1 items
- `~/mikeshaffer/scripts/healthcheck.sh` — Outside-OpenClaw healthcheck (launchd)

### Policy Docs (in workspace, agents read these)
- `~/mikeshaffer/ROUTING.md` — Who goes to Mike vs Maricar vs spam
- `~/mikeshaffer/DRAFTING.md` — Voice rules, AIVA signature rules
- `~/mikeshaffer/MEMORY.md` — Active leads, Oval workflow, business context
- `~/mikeshaffer/TOOLS.md` — Infrastructure references

### State Files
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.action-queue.json` — Current action queue (between scanner and dispatcher)
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.action-queue-archive/` — Processed queue history
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.action-dispatch-ledger.json` — Short-lived ledger of source IDs already handed to async drafters
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.deterministic-action-scanner-state.json` — Last deterministic scan summary
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.scanner-log/` — JSONL scanner run history
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.pending-drafts/` — Drafts awaiting review (one JSON per item)
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.pending-drafts-archive/` — Old drafts
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.draft-history/` — Tracked outcomes (approved, modified, skipped, auto-sent)
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.draft-stats.json` — Aggregated approval rates by channel and action_type
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.email-watcher-state.json` — Tracks surfaced emails to avoid duplicates
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.filter-suggester-state.json` — Tracks proposed Gmail filters
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.mempalace-sync-state.json` — Tracks synced facts to avoid duplicates
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.waiting-on.json` — Dependency chains (managed by `waiton` CLI)
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.auto-sent-log.json` — Log of all Tier 1 auto-sends
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.pending-filter-suggestions.json` — Filter suggestions awaiting approval
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/PUNCH-LIST.md` — System todo list

### Daily Notes
- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` — Per-day notes appended by cron jobs (briefing, watcher, accountability, auto-sent log)

## Cron Schedule (Pacific Time)

| Time | Job | Model | What it does |
|------|-----|-------|--------------|
| 3:00 AM | Memory Dreaming | Native | Promotes durable facts to MEMORY.md (with 30-day temporal decay) |
| 4:00 AM | mempalace-sync | gpt-5.4-mini | Reads MEMORY.md, writes triples to MemPalace knowledge graph |
| 7:30 AM | morning-briefing | gpt-5.4 | Reads everything, sends one consolidated briefing to Google Chat |
| 7:45 AM | action-scanner | glm-5.1 | Runs `action-scan --write --replace`, then dispatches drafters |
| 9:30 AM (M-F) | draft-review-ready | gpt-5.4-mini | Runs auto-sender first, then notifies Mike of pending drafts |
| 9:45/11:45/1:45/3:45 (M-F) | email-watcher | gpt-5.4-mini | Mid-day scans, dependency resolution checks |
| 10:00 AM (M-F) | accountability-check | gpt-5.4-mini | Flags hanging commitments and overdue waiting-on items |
| 2:30 PM (M-F) | email-filter-suggester | gpt-5.4-mini | Proposes Gmail filters for spam/noise |
| Every 30 min | healthcheck | bash + Claude Code | Monitors gateway and cron jobs, fires Claude Code to fix breaks |

## Failure Modes Discovered (and Fixed)

These are all things that have already broken. The fixes are in place but documented here so future-Aiva remembers:

1. **`--at now` fails** — OpenClaw cron requires ISO timestamps, not relative durations. Fixed in dispatcher.
2. **Empty agent output errors** — Agents must produce some text or OpenClaw treats it as an error. Fixed in scanner and review prompts.
3. **Agent tries to use internal `message` tool** — When delivery is "announce", agents shouldn't try to send via tool calls. Fixed in watcher and review prompts.
4. **iMessage hallucination from voicemail phone numbers** — Action scanner had to be told to ONLY queue iMessage items that exist in actual iMessage search results.
5. **iMessage scanner over-eager** — Initial version dumped 37 items including group chats, spam shortcodes, marketing texts. Now filters group chats, shortcodes, toll-free numbers, casual social.
6. **No dispatcher cap** — Original version would create unlimited drafters. Now capped at MAX_DRAFTERS=5.
7. **Agentic scanner fragility** — The old scanner depended on an agent to enumerate channels and emit queue JSON. Replaced with `bin/action-scan` so channel enumeration and queue generation are deterministic, testable, and module-owned.
8. **Async drafter race** — A scanner rerun could rediscover items after dispatcher created one-shot drafters but before draft files existed. Fixed with `.action-dispatch-ledger.json` plus the existing draft/draft-history dedupe.
9. **Emoji-only iMessage IDs** — Emoji/group-chat names collapsed to `imessage-`. Fixed with a stable SHA-256 fallback slug.
10. **Maricar handoff verification missed** — Drafter checked Maricar's sent folder for replies to sender, but not for forwards to relevant third party. Fix pending.

## Integration Points

This pipeline integrates with:

- **dependency-tracker module** — Email watcher checks waiting-on items for resolution; drafters auto-create chains when intermediating
- **mempalace module** — Dreaming sync feeds the knowledge graph; drafters query MemPalace for context
- **google module** — All Gmail send/reply/forward, Google Chat send/read operations
- **imessage module** — iMessage send/read via SSH to laptop
- **calendar module** — Morning briefing reads daily calendar

## Key Behaviors (Read These Before Modifying)

1. **Routing matters more than model power.** Tier 1 routing decisions don't need GPT-5.4. Sending the wrong person doesn't get fixed by a smarter model.

2. **Cross-channel verification is the difference.** Without checking sent folders + iMessages + Maricar's mail + Google Chat, drafters will create work for things Mike already handled.

3. **Limits prevent runaway behavior.** Max 5 in queue, max 5 drafters dispatched, MAX_DRAFTERS hard cap. Always.

4. **Spam gets archived, not routed.** Cold outreach, recruiters, vendor sales pitches do not go to Maricar. They get filtered.

5. **Mike approves Tier 3, AIVA auto-sends Tier 1.** Tier 2 currently goes to review until track record builds.

6. **Customer-facing messages stay in Mike's voice.** Internal Maricar messages get "- AIVA" signature.

## What's NOT Yet Built / Open Items

See `~/mikeshaffer/memory/PUNCH-LIST.md` for the live list. Highlights:

- Weekend personal briefing (Sat/Sun ~8:30 AM)
- Drafter awareness of entity workspaces (`~/mikeshaffer/entities/{slug}/` supplementary files; entity data now from Postgres)
- Multi-attachment Google CLI fix
- Auto-creation of new entity workspaces for new leads
- Bidirectional sync between drafts and entity tasks

## How to Test

### Synthetic test (controlled, fast)
```bash
# Create a test queue item
cat > ~/mikeshaffer/memory/.action-queue.json << 'EOF'
{"items": [{"message_id":"test-X","channel":"route_to_maricar","from":"x@y.com","from_name":"Test Person","subject":"Test inquiry","account":"work","action_type":"route_to_maricar","snippet":"Test scenario","priority":"medium","age_hours":1}]}
EOF
bash ~/mikeshaffer/scripts/dispatch-drafters.sh
# Wait, then check ~/mikeshaffer/memory/.pending-drafts/
```

### Live test (real data)
```bash
openclaw cron run 6451ed93-28b4-4759-abe2-5cddf8a373ad --timeout 900000 --expect-final
# Wait, then check ~/mikeshaffer/memory/.pending-drafts/
```

### Production test

# Conversations Module

Canonical module owner for voice conversation transcripts, speaker identification, and voice memo processing.

Current status:
1. This module is compatibility-first.
2. The live `conversations` CLI implementation now lives in this module.
3. The voice memo watcher, processing scripts, speaker worker, and speaker tools now live in this module.
4. The `voice-memos` and `voice-extract` CLIs now live in this module.
5. The public command surface is generated into `~/.aiva/state/bin` from this module's manifest.
6. Service helpers now live under `modules/conversations/services/`.
7. The public top-level `skills/conversations/SKILL.md` remains hand-owned during migration, while this module also provides a canonical module-local skill doc.

This module now owns the architectural boundary for:
1. transcript database access
2. speaker identification and embedding management
3. voice memo ingestion and watcher logic
4. `voice-memos` and `voice-extract`
5. Phase 1 conversation post-processing through `conversation-pipeline`
6. AIVA-hosted conversations processing
7. Viaim call transcript import into the conversations database

Compatibility notes:
1. Reconcile should not replace the current top-level `conversations` skill while it remains hand-owned.
2. Launchd and operator references should point at `modules/conversations/services/*`.
3. Akaunting and other tooling must read the canonical runtime data from the Supabase Postgres tables listed above, not from any SQLite path. The `~/.aiva/state/conversations/` directory still holds non-DB state (logs, watcher bookkeeping, postprocess outputs) but no longer contains a live database file.

Migration intent:
1. keep current conversations behavior stable
2. establish `conversations` as the canonical feature owner
3. keep runtime state outside the repo-owned module tree
4. move remaining docs and operator surfaces under module ownership in later isolated steps

## Operations — READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING

### Pipeline overview

```
iPhone (Voice Memos) → iCloud → Laptop → rsync → AIVA disk → watcher → AssemblyAI → Postgres
Viaim app (macOS) → local Notekit call.db → sync_viaim.py → Postgres
```

- Voice memos recorded on iPhone sync to laptop via iCloud
- `sync_voice_memos_to_aiva.sh` rsyncs from laptop to AIVA
- `voice_memo_watcher.py` runs via launchd, detects new files, calls `process_voice_memo.py`
- `process_voice_memo.py` loads `speaker_id.py`, which uploads to AssemblyAI for transcription + speaker ID
- Results go into Supabase Postgres (tables: `conversations`, `conversation_turns`, `speakers`, `conversations_speakers`, `speaker_verifications`, `voice_training`, `speaker_jobs`, `voice_embeddings`)
- `sync_viaim.py` reads Viaim's local SQLite database at
  `~/Library/Containers/com.viaim.notekit/Data/Documents/CallRecord/call.db`
  and imports available call transcripts into the same Postgres tables

**Storage backend (since 2026-05-15):** Postgres-only. The legacy SQLite file at
`~/.aiva/state/conversations/conversations.db` has been renamed to
`conversations.db.deprecated-pg-only-2026-05-15` and is no longer read or
written. All callers (in-module and downstream) go through the
`get_pg_conn()` helper defined at the top of `services/speaker_id.py` and
mirrored in the other service files.

### Launchd service

Plist: `~/.aiva/ops/launchd/com.aiva.voice-memos.plist`

**CRITICAL:** The plist MUST have `EnvironmentVariables` with PATH including `/usr/local/bin` — launchd runs with a minimal PATH and `ffprobe`/`ffmpeg` live in `/usr/local/bin`. Without this, pydub and ffprobe calls silently fail.

**CRITICAL:** `ProgramArguments` uses `aiva-python3` which MUST be a symlink to a real python binary (e.g. pyenv 3.10.13), NOT a bash wrapper script. macOS kernel cannot chain shebangs (script → script → binary). If `aiva-python3` is a bash script, any Python CLI that uses it as a shebang will fail with `Exec format error` when called via `subprocess.run()`.

### Viaim sync service

Plist: `~/.aiva/ops/launchd/com.aiva.viaim-sync.plist`

Runs every 15 minutes on AIVA and calls
`~/.aiva/modules/conversations/services/sync_viaim.py`. The sync is
conservative: it imports missing Viaim calls, fills in transcripts that
arrive after the initial metadata import, and inserts only missing stable
utterances by default. It does not overwrite edited conversation titles
or edited utterance speaker names unless run manually with `--force`.

Common commands:

```bash
~/.aiva/modules/conversations/services/sync_viaim.py --status
~/.aiva/modules/conversations/services/sync_viaim.py --record-id <viaim-record-id>
~/.aiva/modules/conversations/services/sync_viaim.py --dry-run
```

### State files

- `~/.aiva/state/conversations/.known_memos` — filenames the watcher has seen and successfully handled. If a memo is in this file, the watcher skips it. If processing fails but the memo gets added here anyway, it's stuck forever.
- `~/.aiva/state/conversations/.claims/` — coordination files for multi-machine claim dedup
- `~/.aiva/state/conversations/postprocess/` — Phase 1 post-processing prompts, structured JSON results, and idempotency run log.
- `~/.aiva/state/conversations/.viaim_sync_state.json` — Viaim source
  record signatures and import bookkeeping for the scheduled sync.

### Phase 1 post-processing

`conversation-pipeline` runs the observation-only post-processing layer after a transcript lands in the DB:

1. resolve the conversation context from hints, entity files, and `~/officeadmin-site/*/index.html` prep pages
2. load the matching entity dossier from Postgres via EntityStore (supplementary files from `~/mikeshaffer/entities/<slug>/` still read for session notes and work records)
3. parse the transcript into structured JSON using Claude Code CLI when available, with a conservative heuristic fallback
4. write the full summary to `~/mikeshaffer/memory/conversation-summaries/`
5. optionally speak the headline through `talk --phone-speak` when confidence clears the configured threshold

It does not write estimates, reminders, open loops, job records, or customer-facing drafts. Those are later phases.

Common commands:

```bash
conversation-pipeline run latest --entity jason-madsen --plan ~/officeadmin-site/jason/index.html
conversation-pipeline scan --since-hours 24 --limit 5
conversation-pipeline status
```

### Known failure modes (things that have broken before)

1. **`aiva-python3` is a bash wrapper instead of a symlink** → pydub/speaker_id imports fail with `ModuleNotFoundError` because the wrapper invokes system Python (3.9) instead of pyenv Python (3.10.13 with deps installed). Fix: `ln -sf ~/.pyenv/versions/3.10.13/bin/python3 ~/.aiva/state/bin/aiva-python3`

2. **Launchd PATH missing `/usr/local/bin`** → ffprobe not found → pydub conversion fails → processing fails. Fix: add `EnvironmentVariables` dict with PATH to the plist.

3. **Memos stuck in `.known_memos` but not in DB** → Old watcher code (before March 2026) marked memos as known even on failure. Current code only marks on success. To unstick: remove the filename from `.known_memos` and the watcher will reprocess on next cycle.

4. **AssemblyAI rejects audio ("no spoken audio")** → `process_voice_memo.py` has safe retry logic that returns True (marks known, stops retrying) for API-processed errors. It only retries on network/transient failures. Permanent failures send a notification to Mike.

### Dependencies

`speaker_id.py` requires: `pydub`, `requests`, `psycopg2`, `numpy`, `assemblyai` API key (in keychain), Supabase Postgres credentials (in keychain: `supabase-aiva-project-ref` and `supabase-aiva-db-password`), `modal` endpoint for the speaker-embedding service. All must be installed in the python that `aiva-python3` points to. Pinecone has been decommissioned; embeddings live in the Postgres `voice_embeddings` table with pgvector.

### Debugging checklist

1. Check watcher is running: `launchctl list | grep voice-memos`
2. Check logs: `tail ~/.aiva/ops/logs/conversations/watcher_stdout.log`
3. Check errors: `tail ~/.aiva/ops/logs/conversations/watcher_stderr.log`
4. Check file counts: watcher logs `Current: X, Known: Y, New: Z` every cycle
5. If `New: 0` but files are missing from DB, check `.known_memos` for stuck entries
6. Test python env: `aiva-python3 -c "import pydub; print('ok')"`
7. Test ffprobe: `aiva-python3 -c "import subprocess; subprocess.run(['ffprobe', '-version'])"`
8. Check Viaim import status:
   `~/.aiva/modules/conversations/services/sync_viaim.py --status`
9. Check Viaim sync logs:
   `tail ~/.aiva/ops/logs/conversations/viaim_sync_stdout.log`

# Dependency Tracker Module

Date: 2026-04-16

## Purpose

Tracks chains where Mike is waiting on one person's reply before he can respond to someone else. These are the balls that get dropped when a subcontractor, vendor, or team member is slow to respond and the original client question ages out of Mike's working memory.

It owns:
1. The `waiton` CLI for managing dependency chains
2. The `dependency-tracker` skill surface
3. The data file at `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.waiting-on.json`

It integrates with:
1. The email watcher cron job (checks incoming mail/iMessages for resolved dependencies)
2. The accountability check cron job (flags stale dependencies for follow-up)
3. The draft response system (dispatches drafters when dependencies resolve)

## How It Works

A dependency chain has these parts:
- **waiting_on**: The person Mike is waiting to hear back from
- **about**: What Mike asked them
- **then_reply_to**: Who Mike needs to get back to once he has the answer
- **follow_up_after_hours**: When to start nudging if no reply

The email watcher checks for incoming replies from anyone Mike is waiting on. When it finds one, the chain resolves and a drafter gets dispatched with the full context to draft a response to the original person.

The accountability check flags chains that have exceeded their follow-up window and offers to nudge the person.

## Public Surface

1. `bin/waiton` - CLI for managing dependencies
2. `bin/draft-tracker` - CLI for tracking draft dependencies and review queues
3. `skill/SKILL.md` - Skill file for agent sessions

# docs module

System documentation for AIVA and OpenClaw. This module is the canonical
source of truth for how the whole system works. Every other agent working on
this codebase should read from and write to this module.

## Status

This module is always a work in progress. As the system changes, docs here
drift from reality. Every document in `content/` carries a header with three
fields:

- `status:` — always `work-in-progress`
- `last-verified:` — ISO date when someone confirmed the doc matches reality
- `confidence:` — `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, or `LOW`

`HIGH` means the author checked the source code, ran the commands, read the
configs, and the doc reflects what they observed. `MEDIUM` means the author
read enough to be confident in the shape but not every detail. `LOW` means
the doc is a sketch or placeholder that has not been verified against the
system and should not be trusted as a reference.

New docs default to `LOW`. A doc moves up only after someone does the
verification work and writes what they checked into the verification log
at `content/VERIFICATION-LOG.md`.

## Files

- `MODULE.md` — this file.
- `module.json` — module manifest.
- `skill/SKILL.md` — instructions for agents on how to use and maintain
  these docs.
- `content/` — the actual documentation tree. Each file is a focused topic
  that links out to existing spec docs, module READMEs, and implementation
  files rather than duplicating them.

## Maintenance rules

1. When any agent changes something about AIVA or OpenClaw, update the
   relevant doc in `content/` in the same change.
2. When a doc is read and found to still be accurate, bump its
   `last-verified` date and note the check in `VERIFICATION-LOG.md`.
3. When a doc is found to be wrong, fix it or mark it `confidence: LOW`
   until fixed.
4. Never delete a doc. Archive outdated docs under
   `content/archive/YYYY-MM-DD/`.
5. Never truncate or summarize away content during edits. Add, correct,
   or mark stale. Do not remove.

# Email Labeler Module

Date: 2026-04-23

## Purpose

`email-labeler` owns local Gmail classification and Gmail-to-Stalwart
archive sync tooling.

It exists for two related but distinct jobs:

1. **Additive Gmail labeling.** Classify Gmail messages locally and apply
   only additive `auto/*` labels. It never archives, deletes, marks read,
   removes labels, or truncates message content.
2. **Local email archive sync.** Mirror Gmail message changes into the
   local Stalwart archive while preserving full RFC822 bytes, attachments,
   and Gmail label semantics.

## Public surface

Module-owned executable scripts live in `bin/`:

- `email-labeler.py` — local Gmail classifier using the Google CLI and
  local model/image processing.
- `email-labeler-stalwart.py` — Stalwart-oriented classifier tooling.
- `gmail-to-stalwart-sync.py` — incremental Gmail history sync into the
  local Stalwart archive.
- `gmail-api-backfill.py` — resumable Gmail API backfill into Stalwart.
- `gmail-api-backfill-threaded.py` — parallel Gmail API backfill.
- `gmail-stalwart-sync-runner.sh` — launchd runner that syncs work and
  personal accounts sequentially.

The reconciled command surface should expose wrapper names without
`.py` where appropriate:

- `email-labeler`
- `email-labeler-stalwart`
- `gmail-to-stalwart-sync`
- `gmail-api-backfill`
- `gmail-api-backfill-threaded`

## Runtime

- Machine: `aiva`.
- Launchd: `com.aiva.gmail-stalwart-sync`.
- Runner: `~/.aiva/modules/email-labeler/bin/gmail-stalwart-sync-runner.sh`.
- Interval observed on 2026-04-23: every 300 seconds.
- State:
  - `~/.aiva/state/email-labeler/`
  - `~/.aiva/state/email-labeler-stalwart/`
  - `~/.aiva/state/gmail-to-stalwart-sync/`
- Logs:
  - `~/.aiva/ops/logs/email-labeler/`
  - `~/.aiva/ops/logs/gmail-to-stalwart-sync/`

## Dependencies

- `google` module and its configured Gmail access for work and personal
  accounts.
- Local Stalwart IMAP server reachable from aiva.
- Local model/runtime dependencies used by the labeler path, including
  Ollama model availability when running `email-labeler.py`.
- Python runtime via `~/.aiva/state/bin/aiva-python3` or the configured
  fallback Python.

## Source-of-truth boundaries

- Gmail remains the source of truth for live email.
- Stalwart is the local archive mirror.
- State files under `~/.aiva/state/` track sync cursors, processed
  message ids, scratch files, and resumable backfill progress.
- This module owns code, runner scripts, and docs only. It does not own
  Gmail account configuration or the Stalwart server itself.

## Safety rules

- No destructive Gmail actions in this module. Labeling is additive.
- No content caps when archiving. Preserve full RFC822 bytes,
  attachments, and labels.
- Do not expose archive credentials in docs or chat output. Move runtime
  secrets toward Keychain or launchd-managed secret injection over time.
- Backfill and incremental sync must be resumable and idempotent.

## Production-readiness notes

This module was registered on 2026-04-23 after the docs drift checker
found live files under `~/.aiva/modules/email-labeler/` without a
`module.json` or `MODULE.md`.

Follow-up hardening:

1. Move Stalwart sync credentials out of inline runner configuration and
   into a Keychain-backed or otherwise centrally managed secret path.
2. Add an explicit restore/read verification command for the archive.
3. Document the Stalwart server owner, data path, backup path, and
   disaster recovery procedure.
4. Add health-check output that proves the sync cursor advances and IMAP
   append/search operations work.

Date: 2026-05-07

## Purpose

`grandma` is the remote-control module for Mike's grandmother's Mac (formerly the 2019 16" MBP that hosted AIVA).

It owns:
1. The `grandma` CLI for one-shot remote operations
2. The `grandma` skill surface
3. SSH/VNC convenience over Tailscale

It does not own:
1. Setup / bootstrap of her Mac (one-time, see `~/grandma-setup-final.sh`)
2. The watchdog daemon on her box (already installed at `/usr/local/bin/grandma-watchdog.sh`)
3. Tailscale auth keys or rotation policy

1. `bin/grandma` (CLI)

- Tailscale hostname `grandma-mac` (IP `100.79.213.1`)
- SSH alias `grandma` in `~/.ssh/config`, key `~/.ssh/aiva_laptop`
- Plain OpenSSH on her box (Tailscale's `--ssh` flag was disabled because it triggered web auth)

- Remote Login enabled (port 22)
- System sleep disabled (display sleep allowed at 15 min)

1. Generate a new reusable, pre-approved Tailscale auth key in admin console
2. `grandma rotate-key tskey-auth-NEW...` (writes it to `/usr/local/etc/grandma-watchdog.authkey`)
3. Watchdog will use the new key on the next disconnect

# Identity Resolver Module

Date: 2026-04-19

## Purpose

The `identity` module is the bridge between AIVA's separate entity stores. It takes any reference to a person or company (a CRM slug, a MemPalace ID, an email, a phone number, a QuickBooks customer ID, an Apple contact ID, a GitHub username, or a free-form display name) and returns one canonical record with every known alias.

It is Phase 1 of the Unified Entity Graph Plan at `~/mikeshaffer/memory/UNIFIED-ENTITY-GRAPH-PLAN.md`.

## What it owns

1. The `identity` CLI for ad-hoc resolution from the shell.
2. The `lib/identity.py` module that other AIVA code imports.
3. The overrides file at `config/overrides.json` where Mike records manual alias mappings for cases the fuzzy matcher cannot figure out on its own.

## What it does NOT own

1. It does not modify the CRM entity folders.
2. It does not modify the MemPalace database.
3. It does not do embedding-based fuzzy matching yet. That is a Phase 4 concern. For now it is string normalization plus a manual overrides file.
4. It does not own QB sync, Contacts sync, or any of the other integrations. Those integrations import this module as a library when they need to bridge IDs.

## Operating Model

One function, `resolve(anything)`, that returns a `CanonicalIdentity` record:

```python
from identity import resolve

rec = resolve("jason-madsen")       # CRM slug
rec = resolve("jason_madsen")        # MemPalace ID
rec = resolve("jason@example.com")   # email
rec = resolve("+1 555 123 4567")     # phone
rec = resolve("Jason Madsen")        # display name
# All five return the same CanonicalIdentity record
```

The record always has at least these fields:

- `canonical_slug`: the CRM-style dashed slug, which AIVA treats as the primary key. If the lookup matched only in MemPalace and no CRM entry exists, this is the best-effort dashed version of the MemPalace ID.
- `mempalace_id`: the underscored MemPalace ID if one is known, otherwise None.
- `display_name`: a human-readable name. Pulls from CRM `entity.json` first, falls back to MemPalace `name`, finally falls back to a title-cased version of the slug.
- `match_type`: a short string like `exact_crm_slug`, `exact_mempalace_id`, `email`, `phone`, `naive_transform`, `name_normalization`, `override`, or `none`. Useful for debugging and for logging confidence downstream.
- `sources`: list of the stores the identity was found in. Subset of `['crm', 'mempalace']` for Phase 1.
- `aliases`: dict of all known identifiers by kind, e.g. `{"crm_slug": "jason-madsen", "mempalace_id": "jason_madsen", "emails": [...], "phones": [...]}`.

If nothing matches, `resolve()` returns `None`. Callers must handle that.

## Resolution Order

1. If the input is already a known CRM slug: return the CRM record (with MemPalace ID added if present).
2. If the input is already a known MemPalace ID: return that record (with CRM slug added if present).
3. If the input looks like an email: delegate to the existing `~/.aiva/modules/mikeshaffer/bin/resolver.py` which already does email → CRM slug. If that hits, continue with step 1.
4. If the input looks like a phone number: same path through the existing resolver.
5. If the input is in the overrides file: use the mapped canonical slug and continue with step 1.
6. Naive dash ↔ underscore transform: if the input is `foo-bar`, try `foo_bar` in MemPalace (and vice versa).
7. Name-normalization: strip all non-alphanumeric characters, lowercase, and look up by normalized name in both stores.
8. If nothing works, return None.

## Overrides file

`config/overrides.json` is hand-maintained. Format:

```json
{
  "nano": { "canonical_slug": "nano", "mempalace_id": "nano_tissera" },
  "don-bozem": { "canonical_slug": "don-bozem", "mempalace_id": "don" },
  "shaffer-construction": {
    "canonical_slug": "shaffer-construction",
    "mempalace_id_aliases": ["shaffer_construction", "shaffer_construction,_inc."]
  }
}
```

Overrides always win. When the resolver detects an ambiguous name match during normal operation (two MemPalace entities whose normalized name collides with one CRM slug), it does not guess. It returns a record with `match_type = "ambiguous"` and a list of candidates, and logs the ambiguity so Mike can add an override.

## Non-goals for Phase 1

- Writing back to MemPalace. The resolver is read-only.
- Merging MemPalace duplicates. The data quality work (1,991 unknown-typed entities, `shaffer_construction` vs. `shaffer_construction,_inc.`) is a separate task tracked in the plan.
- Embedding-based name matching. Deferred to Phase 4.
- Resolving QuickBooks customer IDs, Apple contact IDs, GitHub usernames. Hooks exist in the record schema (`aliases`) but no resolution paths yet.

## Testing

Tests live at `tests/test_identity.py`. They exercise the naive transform, the name-normalization path, the overrides file, ambiguous matches, and the no-match case. Run with `pytest ~/.aiva/modules/identity/tests/`.

## CLI

```bash
identity resolve "jason-madsen"        # pretty output
identity resolve "jason_madsen" --json  # machine-readable
identity list --unmatched-crm          # CRM entities with no MemPalace record
identity list --unmatched-mempalace    # MemPalace entities with no CRM record
identity overrides list
identity overrides add <canonical_slug> <mempalace_id>
```

## Related

- `~/mikeshaffer/memory/UNIFIED-ENTITY-GRAPH-PLAN.md` is the roadmap.
- `~/.aiva/modules/mikeshaffer/bin/resolver.py` is the existing email/phone → CRM resolver. Identity delegates to it for those two input types and preserves its behavior.

# Instagram Module

Read and respond to Instagram DMs. Forward incoming DMs into iMessage so Mike sees them inline.

## Status: Setup In Progress

Gateway binary is built, MCP server deps installed, module scaffolded. Needs session cookies to go live.

## Architecture

Two approaches are available. The active one uses session cookies (no Meta approval needed).

### Active: Cookie-Based MCP Server (instagram-dms-mcp)

```
Go gateway (ig-gateway)  ← talks to Instagram's private API via session cookies
       ↓
Python MCP server        ← exposes get_inbox, get_conversation, send_message, react
       ↓
AIVA MCP config          ← AIVA calls tools directly
       ↓
inject_queue/            ← DM polling drops messages as [IG DM from @user]: "text"
       ↓
responder                ← AIVA processes like any other message
```

**Location:** `modules/instagram/mcp-server/`
**Binary:** `mcp-server/gateway/ig-gateway` (pre-built, Go 1.22+)
**Server:** `mcp-server/src/server.py`
**Port:** MCP server on 8000, gateway on 29391

### Alternate: Official Meta Graph API (requires App Review)

```
webhook_server.py  ← Meta pushes DM events here (port 7790)
       ↓
inject_queue/      ← formatted as [IG DM from @user]: "text"
       ↓
responder          ← AIVA processes like any other message
```

**Location:** `modules/instagram/services/webhook_server.py`, `api.py`, `oauth_server.py`
**Meta App:** "Shaffercon.com-IG" (App ID: 441169528846834)
**Redirect URI:** `https://aiva.officeadmin.io/instagram/callback`
**Cloudflare tunnel:** `aiva.officeadmin.io` → `localhost:7791` (already configured)

Required Meta permissions (Advanced Access, requires app review):
- `instagram_business_basic`
- `instagram_business_content_publish`
- `instagram_business_manage_comments`
- `instagram_business_manage_messages`

## Setup: Cookie-Based (Current)

### Step 1: Get Instagram Session Cookies

1. Go to instagram.com in a browser, log in
2. Open DevTools (Cmd+Option+I) → Application → Cookies → `https://www.instagram.com`
3. Copy these 6 values:
   - `sessionid`
   - `ds_user_id`
   - `csrftoken`
   - `datr`
   - `ig_did`
   - `mid`

### Step 2: Store Cookies

```bash
# Store in Keychain (preferred)
security add-generic-password -s "instagram-cookies" -a "mikejshaffer" -w '{"sessionid":"...","ds_user_id":"...","csrftoken":"...","datr":"...","ig_did":"...","mid":"..."}'

# Or set as env vars
export IG_SESSION_ID="..."
export IG_USER_ID="..."
export IG_CSRF_TOKEN="..."
export IG_DATR="..."
export IG_DID="..."
export IG_MID="..."
```

### Step 3: Test the MCP Server

```bash
cd ~/.aiva/modules/instagram/mcp-server
python3 src/server.py
# Should print "Gateway ready - logged in as @yourusername"
```

### Step 4: Add to AIVA MCP Config

Add to `.mcp.json` or equivalent:
```json
{
  "instagram-dms": {
    "command": "python3",
    "args": ["~/.aiva/modules/instagram/mcp-server/src/server.py"],
    "env": {
      "IG_SESSION_ID": "<from keychain>",
      "IG_USER_ID": "<from keychain>",
      "IG_CSRF_TOKEN": "<from keychain>"
    }
  }
}
```

### Step 5: Wire DM Polling into iMessage

Modify `mcp-server/src/server.py` to write to AIVA's inject queue instead of Poke webhook:
- Replace the `flush_pending_messages` Poke POST with a JSON write to `~/.aiva/state/responder/inject_queue/`
- Format: `{"sender": "+13105969154", "text": "[Instagram DM from @user]: message", "source": "instagram"}`

## Setup: Official Meta API (Deferred)

### Step 1: Get App Review Approval

1. Go to [developers.facebook.com/apps/441169528846834](https://developers.facebook.com/apps/441169528846834)
2. Under App Review → Permissions and Features, request Advanced Access for `instagram_business_manage_messages`
3. Submit use case (customer support / business messaging)
4. Wait for approval (days to weeks)

### Step 2: Run OAuth Flow

```bash
cd ~/.aiva/modules/instagram
python3 oauth_server.py
# Opens auth URL, captures callback, stores long-lived token in Keychain
```

### Step 3: Start Webhook Server

```bash
python3 services/webhook_server.py
# Listens on port 7790, receives Meta webhook events
```

### Step 4: Register Webhook in Meta Dashboard

1. Go to Meta Developer Dashboard → Your App → Webhooks
2. Callback URL: `https://aiva.officeadmin.io/instagram/webhook` (needs tunnel route update to 7790)
3. Verify Token: stored in Keychain under `instagram-webhook` / `verify_token`
4. Subscribe to: `messages`

## CLI

```bash
instagram read                    # recent DMs across all accounts
instagram read @username          # DMs with specific user
instagram send @username "text"   # send a DM
instagram accounts                # list connected accounts
instagram setup                   # configure OAuth tokens (official API)
```

## File Map

```
modules/instagram/
  module.json                    # module manifest
  MODULE.md                      # this file
  api.py                         # Meta Graph API client (official API path)
  oauth_server.py                # OAuth callback server (official API path)
  bin/instagram                  # CLI
  services/
    webhook_server.py            # Meta webhook listener (official API path)
  skills/instagram/
    SKILL.md                     # Claude skill definition
  mcp-server/                    # Cookie-based MCP approach (active)
    gateway/
      ig-gateway                 # Pre-built Go binary
      build.sh                   # Rebuild with: cd gateway && ./build.sh
      cmd/                       # Go source
      pkg/                       # Go source
    src/
      server.py                  # FastMCP server
    requirements.txt             # Python deps: fastmcp, httpx, python-dotenv
```

## Credentials

| Item | Location |
|------|----------|
| Meta App ID | `441169528846834` |
| Meta App Secret | Keychain: `instagram-app` / `app_secret` |
| IG Session Cookies | Keychain: `instagram-cookies` / `mikejshaffer` (not yet stored) |
| Webhook Verify Token | Keychain: `instagram-webhook` / `verify_token` (generated during setup) |
| Cloudflare Tunnel | `aiva.officeadmin.io` → `localhost:7791` |

## Risks & Notes

- Cookie-based approach: cookies expire periodically, Instagram may flag automation. Use a dedicated account if possible.
- Official API: 24-hour messaging window (resets when user responds), 200 DM/hr rate limit, requires Business/Creator account.
- Both approaches only work with accounts Mike controls. Can't read DMs from arbitrary accounts.

# know

Date: 2026-05-16

## Purpose

`know` is the unified knowledge front-end. One CLI that resolves a reference (email, phone, slug, display name), fans out across every knowledge backend in parallel, and returns a merged dossier with a synthesized status header at the top.

It owns:
1. The `know` CLI surface (main dossier command + cross-entity views)
2. Reference resolution: email / phone / slug / name (with loose matching and via-org fallback for unknown senders at known domains)
3. Parallel fan-out and per-backend timeouts
4. The synthesis layer: derives `headline`, `last_action` (channel + direction + date), `waiting_on` (inferred from commitments + most-recent message direction), and per-backend counts
5. Output modes: full markdown (default), `--brief` compact summary, `--json` structured
6. Caching of dossiers (5-minute TTL)
7. The `--summarize` LLM synthesis layer (off by default; see SKILL.md for rules)

It does not own:
1. Any underlying knowledge data. Each backend remains the source of truth for its data.
2. Backend-specific CRUD beyond passthroughs. Use the backend's own CLI (or `notes`, `mempalace`, etc.) for admin work.

## Public Surface

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `know <ref>` | Full dossier across all 15 backends |
| `know <ref> --brief` | Compact summary (synthesis header, counts, workspace docs, pending drafts), no raw backend dumps |
| `know <ref> --json` | Structured JSON for agents |
| `know <ref> -b <backend>` | Filter to one backend |
| `know --waiting-on-me` | Open commitments where Mike owes the next move |
| `know --waiting-on-them` | Open commitments where the other party owes the next move |
| `know --active --days N` | Entities whose workspace files were touched in the last N days |
| `know search <query>` | Free-text search across backends |
| `know tasks <ref>` | Tasks for an entity |
| `know commitments <...>` | Passthrough to commitments CLI |
| `know entities <...>` | Passthrough to entities CLI |
| `know graph <...>` | Passthrough to mempalace CLI |
| `know notes <...>` | Passthrough to notes CLI |
| `know voice <...>` | Passthrough to conversations CLI |
| `know sessions <...>` | Passthrough to session-search CLI |
| `know calls <...>` | Passthrough to aiva callhistory |

## Backends `know` delegates to

Core (always queried):

| Backend | Source | What it provides |
|---|---|---|
| entities | `mikeshaffer` entity store | Structured records on people, orgs, pets, vehicles, places, projects |
| graph | `mempalace` | Bi-temporal triples from the knowledge graph |
| notes | `notes` | Apple Notes content (text search) |
| voice | `conversations` | Voice memo transcripts with speaker ID |
| sessions | `session-search` | Cross-machine session log search |

Entity-scoped (queried once the ref is resolved to an entity, using its emails / phones / display name):

| Backend | Source | What it provides |
|---|---|---|
| commitments | `commitments` | Open and historical commitments where Mike or the entity owes the next move |
| calls | `callhistory` | Recent matching calls |
| drafts | `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.pending-drafts/` | Every pending draft queued for this sender (by entity_slug or from-email match). Critical for dedup. |
| gmail | `google gmail` (work + personal) | Up to 15 recent Gmail threads to/from any of this entity's emails |
| imessage | `imessage thread <phone>` | Last ~12 messages in the iMessage thread for each entity phone |
| calendar | `google raw calendar events list` (work + personal) | Calendar events from the last 14d + next 30d involving this entity by name / email / location |
| quickbooks | `quickbooks get-customer`, `search-estimates`, `search-invoices` | Customer record + 10 most recent estimates and invoices (only when entity has `quickbooks_customer_id`) |
| chat | `google chat read` | Recent Maricar↔Mike Google Chat messages mentioning this entity |
| reminders | `reminders search` | macOS Reminders matching this entity name |
| files | local filesystem | Listing of `entities/<slug>/` plus markdown excerpts (BID-STATUS.md, WALK-NOTE-*.md, etc.) up to 3 levels deep |

The underlying CLIs are kept alive. `know` calls them via subprocess. Agents should default to `know`; reach for a backend CLI directly only when you need a write or admin op that doesn't fit the unified surface.

## Synthesis

Every dossier includes a `synthesis` field computed locally from the backend results. It contains:

- `headline`: a one-line status string (e.g. "waiting on Mike (last_gmail_inbound); last gmail 2026-05-15 ← them; 2 pending draft(s)")
- `waiting_on`: `{who: "mike"|"them", basis: "open_commitment"|"last_gmail_inbound"|...}` inferred from open commitments first, then from the direction of the most recent message
- `last_action`: `{channel, direction (mike|them), date, snippet}` across gmail / imessage / calls
- `counts`: per-backend counts (gmail_threads, open_drafts, open_commitments_mike_owes, etc.)
- `workspace_docs`: paths of any *.md files in the entity workspace
- `open_commitment_subjects`, `open_draft_subjects`

The synthesis is cheap (no extra I/O) and always included. Agents should read it before walking individual backend payloads.

## Resolution

Resolution flow: ref → `entities resolve <ref>` → canonical slug. Supports:

- Email: `know nung@charlesdunn.com` → `nathan-ung`
- Phone (any format): `know +16263765528` → `nathan-ung`
- Slug: `know nathan-ung`
- Display name with loose matching: `know "Charles Dunn"` → `charlesdunn` (lowercases + strips punctuation for matching)
- Via-org fallback: `know stranger@charlesdunn.com` → `charlesdunn` (org) when no person matches but the domain is a known org

When multiple entities match a name, `know` returns the candidates list and asks the caller to disambiguate.

## Architecture

Single Python script at `/Users/mikeshaffer/.aiva/state/bin/know`. Fan-out via ThreadPoolExecutor with per-backend timeouts:

- entities: 30s
- graph: 20s, notes: 15s, voice: 15s, sessions: 20s
- commitments: 15s, calls: 20s
- drafts: 5s (local filesystem)
- gmail: 25s, imessage: 15s
- calendar: 20s
- quickbooks: 20s
- chat: 20s, reminders: 10s, files: 5s

Caching is in-memory per-process (LRU keyed by ref + backend) with a 5-minute TTL. Use `--no-cache` or `--refresh` to bypass.

## Operating Model

This module is machine-local but read-only-from-anywhere:
1. `know` runs on whichever machine invokes it, calls local backend CLIs in parallel
2. The `sessions` backend handles cross-machine via session-search's existing SSH delegation
3. No daemon, no service, no port. Just a CLI that runs on demand.

## Related

- CLI: `/Users/mikeshaffer/.aiva/state/bin/know` (single Python file)
- Agent skill: `skill/SKILL.md` (canonical reference for agents)
- Spec: `~/mikeshaffer/KNOWLEDGE_MODEL.md` (older design doc; some sections superseded by current implementation)

# macOS Automator

Wraps the [`@steipete/macos-automator-mcp`](https://github.com/steipete/macos-automator-mcp) MCP server as a standalone AIVA CLI. Lets agents run AppleScript or JXA against any Mac app (Finder, Safari, Chrome, Terminal, Mail, Notes, Calendar, Keynote, Xcode, etc.) and browse a 490+ entry knowledge base of pre-built scripts.

## How it was built

Generated from the upstream MCP server using `mcporter generate-cli --compile`:

```
mcporter generate-cli --server macos-automator --compile ~/.aiva/modules/macos-automator/bin/macos-automator
```

The compiled binary is a self-contained Bun-built arm64 Mach-O executable. It spawns the npx-distributed MCP server under the hood for each invocation, so the first run on a fresh machine downloads `@steipete/macos-automator-mcp@latest` via npm.

To regenerate after an upstream release, rerun the same `generate-cli --compile` command.

## Commands

`macos-automator` exposes two subcommands, mirroring the MCP tools:

- `macos-automator execute-script` — run inline AppleScript/JXA (`--script-content`), a script file (`--script-path`), or a knowledge-base script by id (`--kb-script-id`). Supports `--language applescript|javascript`, `--arguments`, plus `--raw <json>` for advanced fields like `input_data`, `timeout_seconds`, `output_format_mode`.
- `macos-automator get-scripting-tips` — browse the knowledge base. `--list-categories true` for the top-level taxonomy, `--category <name>` to drill in, `--search-term "..."` to fuzzy search across all tips.

Every call prints a stderr banner like `MacOS Automator MCP v0.4.1, started at ...`. That is not an error.

## Host requirements

- macOS (the bundled MCP server only runs on Darwin).
- Node.js >= 24 on `PATH` for the npx-spawned server.
- macOS Privacy & Security permissions for whichever process invokes the CLI (Terminal, iTerm, or the agent's tmux/launchd host):
  - **Automation** → for controlling target apps (System Events, Finder, Safari, etc.). First-time control of a new app triggers a TCC prompt.
  - **Accessibility** → required for UI scripting via System Events.

## Relationship to `osascript-shim`

`osascript-shim` serializes raw `/usr/bin/osascript` calls behind a system-wide flock. This module is a different layer: it runs scripts via the MCP server's own osascript driver, not through the shim. If concurrent AppleScript wedging becomes a problem here, the fix is to add a flock wrapper around this binary's entry, not to route it through the existing shim (which only intercepts the `osascript` command name).

# Memory Module (DEPRECATED)

Date: 2026-03-08
Deprecated: 2026-04-23

## Status

DEPRECATED. The Apple-Notes-backed "Memory" and "Soul" note hydration
pipeline was too slow and painful to maintain from iOS, and Mike does
not need the rendered contents often enough to justify the active
plugin footprint.

What actually happened:

1. `hydrate()` (fetch Memory + Soul notes from Apple Notes, compose
   AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) stopped running in practice. Hydrated files at
   `~/.aiva/state/modules/memory/` froze at 2026-03-09.
2. `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (the file Claude Code actually reads at
   startup) is maintained by hand now, at about 1.3 KB.
3. The `update-memory-date.py` launchd job (`com.aiva.update-claude-date`,
   every 600s) was unloaded 2026-04-23. Its stale "THIS SESSION STARTED
   ON SATURDAY March 7th, 2026" banner showed the job was not keeping
   the date fresh either.

Do not use this module as an active plugin. The hydrated files and
code are preserved in place for potential future revival as a
read-only mirror surfaced through OpenClaw (e.g. as a canvas snapshot
of the Apple Notes Memory and Soul notes) rather than a hot-reload
runtime pipeline.

## Preserved artifacts (do not delete)

- `bin/memory` — legacy CLI
- `bin/update-memory-date.py` — date-banner updater (agent disabled)
- `runtime.py` — the hydrate/read_artifact code path
- `references/memory-module-intent.md` — original design intent
- Hydrated files at `~/.aiva/state/modules/memory/AGENTS.md`,
  `CLAUDE.md`, `sources.json`, `status.json` (frozen 2026-03-09)

## Active consumer to watch

- `~/.aiva/modules/claude/provider.py` still imports
  `read_artifact` from this module. Today that returns the frozen
  March 9 AGENTS.md contents. When we formally remove the module,
  `provider.py` needs to read the maintained file at
  `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` directly (or read nothing and rely on the
  Claude Code runtime to pick up its local CLAUDE.md).

## Original intent (kept for reference)

The sections below describe the original design. They are retained so
a future revival has a clear starting point.

### Purpose (original)

`memory` was the module-owned runtime context hydration layer.

It owned:
1. the source-of-truth memory model for agent identity and long-lived context
2. reading canonical `Memory` and `Soul` notes from Apple Notes via the AIVA contact's linked note IDs
3. rendering hydrated runtime instruction files for agent runtimes
4. hot-reload policy for memory and soul updates
5. `update-memory-date` for keeping hydrated session-date context current

### Source Of Truth (original)

Canonical source of truth lived in Apple Notes only:
1. the note linked as `memory` on the AIVA contact
2. the note linked as `soul` on the AIVA contact

These notes were the only human-maintained source files for this layer.

### Operating Model (original)

Hydration flow:
1. read `memory` and `soul` from the Apple Notes links stored on the AIVA contact
2. compose provider-specific instruction wrappers
3. write hydrated `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` into module state
4. launch or refresh provider runtimes against those hydrated files

Hot reload was the intended behavior:
1. `Memory` edits defaulted to soft reload
2. `Soul` edits defaulted to hard reload

### Why it did not stick

- Editing long multi-section notes on iPhone Notes was slow and error-prone.
- The hydrate path depended on osascript-driven Notes reads that were fragile across macOS versions.
- Claude Code already reads its own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` at startup, so a short hand-maintained file covers the 90% case.

### Revival sketch (not scheduled)

A later iteration could flip this module from active-hydrator to
passive-mirror:

1. OpenClaw (or a similar surface) watches the Apple Notes "Memory"
   and "Soul" notes.
2. On change, it writes a timestamped snapshot under
   `state/modules/memory/history/` and updates a single current
   mirror file.
3. Provider runtimes decide whether to read the mirror. Nothing hot
   reloads automatically.

This preserves Apple Notes as the human edit surface without
requiring a provider pipeline to keep up.

# module-suggester

Background agent that reviews completed AIVA sessions and proposes reusable skills as new modules or updates to existing ones. All processing runs on aiva; proposals land in a staging area colocated with modules/ but deliberately invisible to the module reconciler so nothing auto-ships.

## Layout

```
modules/module-suggester/
  bin/module-suggester            # the CLI (run|list|show|accept|reject|stats)
  lib/
    __init__.py
    scanner.py                  # discover candidate session JSONLs
    seen.py                     # append-only dedupe log
    analyzer.py                 # call Gemini (default) or Claude CLI, parse JSON
    guard.py                    # regex reject-pattern scanner
    proposal.py                 # write/read/validate proposals
    materializer.py             # accept moves files + reconciles; reject archives
  config/
    analyzer-prompt.md          # the system prompt for the analyzer model
    reject-patterns.json        # safety regexes
  skill/SKILL.md                # agent-facing documentation
```

## Staging area

`~/.aiva/modules/.module-suggester-staging/<proposal-id>/`

The dot prefix and depth-2 layout both make this invisible to `modules/*/module.json` glob used by reconcile and validate. Proposals are fully-formed module trees ready to move.

## State

`~/.aiva/state/module-suggester/`

- `seen.jsonl` — append-only log of (session path, mtime, size, model, result)
- `logs/` — one file per day with run output
- `accepted/<id>.PROPOSAL.md` — audit trail of accepted proposals
- `accepted-backups/<timestamp>-<target>/` — original files of update-type accepts, in case we need to revert
- `rejected/<id>/` — archived rejected proposals (full tree preserved)
- `rejected-by-guard/<id>/` — proposals that tripped the safety scanner

## Design choices

**Default backend: Gemini.** The analyzer calls `gemini -p <system-prompt> -o json` with the full session on stdin. 1M-token context means most sessions don't need trimming. The alternative Claude backend (via `claude --print --bare`) is retained as a fallback.

**Conservative trim caps.** Gemini sessions are capped at 1.5MB and Claude sessions at 400KB as defense against pathological session files. Normal sessions are well under these limits.

**Skipped sessions.** The scanner skips files that are smaller than 4KB, modified within the last 5 minutes (may still be writing), older than 14 days (configurable), or already analyzed at their current mtime+size.

**Guard is conservative.** Reject patterns include generic credential shapes, anthropic/openai/aws key prefixes, `rm -rf` on home or root, DROP/TRUNCATE without IF EXISTS, curl-pipe-shell, eval-of-variable, SSL-verify-off, global git config writes, launchctl-wildcard-unload, git-force-push-without-lease, aiva state deletion, and mempalace deletion. False positives are preferred over false negatives. Diverted proposals stay fully readable in `rejected-by-guard/` for inspection.

**No auto-acceptance.** Every proposal waits for `module-suggester accept <id>` or `reject <id>`. This is the explicit design choice Mike made: we build/test/stage, human gates ship.

## Automation

An OpenClaw cron job (`module-suggester-scan`, id `8d73c0b8-2f53-42f0-b4a6-23130b133bd8`) runs every 6 hours in an isolated agent session. The agent invokes `module-suggester run --limit 3 --backend gemini --no-notify`, reviews each pending proposal via `show`, assigns ACCEPT / REVIEW / REJECT verdicts, and then AUTO-EXECUTES every REJECT by calling `module-suggester reject <id>` so those proposals never appear in future Mike-facing reports. The remaining ACCEPT and REVIEW items are delivered to Mike's AIVA bot Google Chat space (`spaces/yueRxUAAAAE`) with the auto-reject list shown once (with reasons) so Mike can veto if he disagrees. Archived rejects live at `state/module-suggester/rejected/<id>/` and can be manually restored. Scheduling + delivery live entirely in OpenClaw; there is no launchd component and no BlueBubbles/iMessage path. The CLI also exposes a `--no-notify` flag for direct invocation that skips any legacy CLI-level notification (which no longer exists).

The timer is optional. Ad-hoc manual usage works fine without it.

## Evolution

- (DONE) Scanner reads laptop-mirrored sessions at `~/laptop-mount/.claude/projects` and `~/laptop-mount/.codex/sessions`, populated every 30min by the existing `com.aiva.mempalace-laptop-sync` launchd agent.
- If we accumulate false-positive guard rejects, tighten patterns in `reject-patterns.json`.
- If Gemini's JSON-envelope format changes or a better flag exists for raw structured output, update `call_gemini` in `analyzer.py`.
- If we want proposal diffing across runs (same session revisited, different proposal), add a `state/module-suggester/history/` keyed by session path.

modules.module_md:
# Open Loops Ledger Module

**Date:** 2026-04-20
**Status:** shipped v1

## Purpose

A single append-only ledger that tracks every active back-and-forth between Mike and another person as a small two-state machine. Answers the one question Mike asks himself all day: "where is the ball right now, on every open conversation?"

Different from the dependency-tracker module (`waiton`). That module tracks specific blocked chains: "waiting on X before I can reply to Y." Open-loops is broader: every open thread, regardless of whether it's blocked on someone else.

## Data model

Single JSONL file at `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.open-loops.jsonl`. One event per line. Append-only. Never deletes, never truncates.

Every event is one of:

- `open` — a new loop opened
- `ball_flip` — the ball moved from one side to the other
- `nudge` — Mike sent a nudge but the ball is still on them
- `note` — free-form note attached to the loop
- `close` — loop resolved

The current state of any loop is derived by replaying its events in order. Two loop states: `waiting_on: mike` or `waiting_on: them`.

## Core shape

```
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "ts": "2026-04-20T10:57:00Z",
  "type": "open | ball_flip | nudge | note | close",
  "loop_id": "slug-or-uuid",          // stable across events in one loop
  "counterparty": "Tina Marie",       // the other person
  "counterparty_id": "+13236109399",  // phone, email, or canonical ref
  "channel": "imessage | email | chat | phone | in-person",
  "subject": "1012 Marion Dr Glendale can lights",  // human-readable
  "waiting_on": "mike | them",        // state AFTER this event
  "reference_id": "ext-id",           // message-id, thread-id, etc.
  "deadline": "2026-04-23",           // optional
  "note": "free-form context",        // optional
  "source": "manual | aiva-handoff | scanner | email-watcher"
}
```

## Public CLI

`open-loops` (also aliased as `loops`):

- `open-loops open --who "Tina Marie" --subject "Marion Dr cans" --waiting-on them` — open a new loop
- `open-loops flip <loop-id> --to mike` — flip the ball
- `open-loops nudge <loop-id>` — record a nudge, ball stays on them
- `open-loops close <loop-id> --reason "resolved"` — close a loop
- `open-loops list` — show all open loops sorted by age on current side
- `open-loops list --waiting-on mike` — only loops where Mike owes a reply
- `open-loops show <loop-id>` — full event history of one loop

`record-commitment`:

- Deterministic wrapper for scanners and per-email processors.
- Writes the same append-only ledger shape as `open-loops open`.
- Idempotent by `reference_id` / `idempotency_key`, or by open loop with the
  same counterparty and subject.
- Preferred LLM usage is stdin JSON:

```
record-commitment --from-stdin-json <<'JSON'
{
  "counterparty": "Maricar",
  "counterparty_id": "maricar@shaffercon.com",
  "subject": "Return Roberts Bros proposal to Alicia",
  "waiting_on": "them",
  "channel": "email",
  "reference_id": "gmail-message-id",
  "deadline": "2026-04-29",
  "note": "Mike forwarded the signed-proposal task to Maricar.",
  "source": "per-email-processor"
}
JSON
```

`project-waiting-on`:

- Deterministic projector from `.open-loops.jsonl` to Apple Reminders list
  `AIVA — Waiting On`.
- Projects only open loops with `waiting_on=them` and `deadline <= today`.
- Keeps future waiting-on state in the ledger only.
- Completing a Waiting On reminder records a `nudge` event in the ledger and
  suppresses re-projection until a newer ledger event appears for that loop.
- Uses state file `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.waiting-on-projector-state.json`.

`follow-through-checker`:

- Applies deterministic evidence rows to the ledger.
- Evidence source:
  `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.follow-through-evidence.jsonl`.
- State file:
  `~/mikeshaffer/memory/.follow-through-state.json`.
- Supported evidence kinds: `counterparty_replied`, `mike_replied`,
  `resolved`, `dependency_satisfied`, `nudge_no_response`, `dismissed`.
- Unit tests cover open, flip-to-Mike, flip-to-them, closed-by-evidence,
  dependency-satisfied, nudge-fired-no-response, and dismissal.

`extract-conversation-commitments`:

- Conservative deterministic extractor for
  `~/.aiva/state/conversations/conversations.db`.
- Skips generic speakers unless the speaker is Mike.
- Uses strong action-verb patterns, then calls `record-commitment`.
- Scheduled through launchd every 15 minutes.

`synthetic-commitment-e2e`:

- Real synthetic test that writes a disposable commitment, runs the
  projector, verifies Reminders creation/idempotency, completes the
  reminder, verifies suppression, and closes the disposable loop.

## Integrations

- `aiva-handoff` writes an `open` event when a handoff is created (`waiting_on: them`).
- Morning briefing reads the ledger and surfaces loops where ball-on-mike is older than N hours at the top of the briefing.
- Waiting On projector reads due `waiting_on=them` loops and mirrors them to
  the `AIVA — Waiting On` Reminders list.
- `record-commitment` lets email processors and future commitment extractors
  write real loop entries without reimplementing ledger rules.
- Follow-through checker applies channel evidence rows back into the ledger.
- Conversations extractor reads viaim / voice memo transcripts from
  `conversations.db` and writes conservative commitments.
- Action-scanner will read the ledger in a future update to avoid re-queueing items that are already tracked.

## Why append-only

Mike's hard rule: never delete data, never truncate. Events accumulate forever. The "current state" of a loop is a projection over its events, not a mutable row. Replay is always possible.

## Public Surface

1. `bin/open-loops` — CLI for managing the ledger
2. `bin/record-commitment` — idempotent writer wrapper for processors
3. `bin/project-waiting-on` — deterministic Reminders projector
4. `bin/follow-through-checker` — applies deterministic evidence rows
5. `bin/extract-conversation-commitments` — conversations.db source
6. `bin/synthetic-commitment-e2e` — real end-to-end validation
7. `bin/verify-commitment-wiring` — prompt/script wiring audit
8. `lib/ledger.py` — Python library for programmatic access (imported by aiva-handoff)
9. `skill/SKILL.md` — Skill file for agent sessions

# opendesk

Screen-aware desktop control for AIVA. Wraps the [`vitalops/opendesk`](https://github.com/vitalops/opendesk) MCP server as a standalone CLI plus a Gemma-driven self-loop wrapper.

## Why this exists alongside `macos-automator`

`macos-automator` is great when an app has a clean AppleScript dictionary or its UI is fully exposed to the Accessibility API. It falls down when:

- A button only appears on hover (the X on a notification banner).
- The relevant control is owned by a non-focused process (Background Task Management banners, Control Center popovers).
- You need to act based on what is *visually* on screen, not what the a11y tree happens to expose.

`opendesk` covers that gap. It can screenshot the screen, overlay numbered Set-of-Marks boxes on every clickable element, OCR arbitrary regions, and drive mouse/keyboard at pixel precision. Same a11y layer underneath for the easy cases, vision + coordinates as a fallback.

## How it was built

The MCP server backend is the upstream JS implementation (`@vitalops/opendesk-sdk`), which is meaningfully more active than the Python side and has its own OCR (tesseract.js based, avoids the Python OCR bug `ocr_image() takes 1 positional argument but 3 were given`).

```
# JS MCP server (used by the compiled CLI and by Claude via mcporter)
cd ~/.aiva/modules/opendesk && npm install @vitalops/opendesk-sdk
mcporter generate-cli --server opendesk --compile bin/opendesk-cli

# Python venv (kept ONLY for the opendesk-gemma OpenAI-compat agent loop)
uv venv ~/.aiva/modules/opendesk/.venv
uv pip install 'opendesk[core,mcp]' openai
```

`~/.mcporter/mcporter.json` points the `opendesk` server at `node_modules/.bin/opendesk-js-mcp`. The compiled CLI is a Bun-built arm64 Mach-O, regenerate with the `mcporter generate-cli` line above after upstream updates (`npm update @vitalops/opendesk-sdk`).

## Tools

17 subcommands mirroring the MCP tools. Most-used:

- `screenshot` — capture screen, optionally with `--marks true` for Set-of-Marks numbered boxes, or `--zoom` to crop.
- `mouse` — move/click/scroll/drag. Always pass `image_width`/`image_height` (via `--raw`) when clicking from a screenshot to get correct Retina coordinate scaling.
- `keyboard` — type strings, press single keys, or send hotkeys like `cmd+w`.
- `app` — open / close / focus / list applications by name.
- `ui` — click/type by Accessibility name (`--action click --app Safari --title "Close"`) — preferred over `mouse` when the element is in the a11y tree.
- `clipboard` — read/write the macOS clipboard.
- `ocr` — extract text from a screen region via Apple Vision or tesseract.
- `learn` — record/replay macro-style procedures.
- `schedule` — register recurring background tasks.

## Gemma self-loop mode

`bin/opendesk-gemma` runs opendesk's standalone OpenAI-compatible agent loop against the local Ollama instance (`http://localhost:11434/v1`, model `gemma4:e4b`).

Use this for short, well-scoped, low-stakes tasks where a small local model is enough:

```
opendesk-gemma "dismiss the notification banner in the top right"
opendesk-gemma "open System Settings, click Notifications, scroll to find Background Task Management"
```

Do **not** use it for multi-step planning or anything that touches important data. 8B Gemma will hallucinate marks, misread the screen, and stall on dialogs. For real work, keep Claude in the driver's seat via MCP mode.

## Gemma terminal helper

`bin/gemma` is a tiny terminal wrapper around the local Ollama Gemma endpoint. It sends whatever Mike types after `gemma`, prints the answer or generated command, and copies the final text to the macOS clipboard.

It defaults to `gemma4:e4b`, matching the lightweight Claude Code wrapper so Ollama can keep one shared model loaded. Set `GEMMA_MODEL` or pass `--model` to use a different tag.

Image files can be attached anywhere in the prompt with `@path/to/image.png`. The wrapper removes the file reference from the text and sends the image bytes to Ollama.

Use `--no-copy` or `--no-clipboard` when calling it from scripts that should only read stdout.

For command style requests, it runs normal zsh commands but blocks a small unsafe executable list in code. Blocked commands are copied, then the CLI prints a note that they are not safe for Gemma to run itself.

## Host requirements

- macOS with Screen Recording + Accessibility granted to the terminal/launchd process that invokes the CLI. Already granted on this machine (confirmed via `opendesk check`).
- Python 3.12 (bundled in the module's `.venv`).
- Ollama running locally with `gemma4:e4b` pulled, for the Gemma loop only.

## Relationship to other modules

- `macos-automator` — use first when you can write the action as AppleScript / JXA / a knowledge-base script. Cheaper and faster than the screenshot loop.
- `opendesk` — reach for this when the target is hover-only, owned by a system agent, or only identifiable by visual position.
- `osascript-shim` — orthogonal. Serializes raw `osascript` calls. Not in the opendesk path.

modules.module_md:
# osascript-shim

Universal serialization wrapper around `/usr/bin/osascript` that prevents concurrent AppleScript calls from wedging macOS automation daemons.

## Why this module exists

`osascript` talks to system automation services like Contacts, Calendar, Mail, Reminders, and Finder. Those services do not handle many simultaneous clients gracefully. When several Claude sessions, cron jobs, or background agents all run `osascript` at once, Apple's daemons (contactsd, CalNCService, etc) can stall or lock up, and the calling processes hang indefinitely.

The shim fixes that by taking an exclusive file lock before running the real `/usr/bin/osascript`. Only one shim-wrapped call executes at a time across the whole machine. Concurrent callers wait for their turn and then proceed in order.

## How it works

The shim is a tiny Swift binary compiled from `src/osascript-shim.swift`. It:

1. Opens a system-wide lock file at `/tmp/osascript-shim.lock`
2. Calls `flock(LOCK_EX)` to block until it holds the lock
3. Execs `/usr/bin/osascript` with the caller's argv intact
4. Releases the lock automatically when the child process exits

Because it is `exec` (not fork + wait), the caller's exit code, stdout, and stderr pass through unchanged. Existing scripts that call `osascript` by name through `$PATH` get serialized transparently.

## Install

A symlink at `~/bin/osascript` points to `bin/osascript` inside this module. `~/bin` is earlier in `$PATH` than `/usr/bin`, so every unqualified `osascript` call goes through the shim. Scripts that explicitly call `/usr/bin/osascript` bypass it, which is occasionally useful when debugging.

## Build

```
swiftc -O src/osascript-shim.swift -o bin/osascript
```

Re-build after any change to the Swift source. The repo commits the compiled binary so fresh checkouts do not need Swift.

## Observability

Lock contention is visible in `ops/logs/osascript-shim/` when needed. A lock wait longer than 30 seconds is worth investigating since it usually means a Contacts or Calendar daemon is itself stuck.

## Related

- `modules/contacts/` uses `osascript` heavily for writes that the CNContactStore API rejects
- `modules/reminders/` uses EventKit directly now, but had an `osascript` path historically
- `modules/imessage/` uses `osascript` for sending on the responder laptop
